Behind This Music: "Black Hole"

"Black Hole" is a song that explores an emotional and existential journey, portraying someone trapped in emptiness—both physically and metaphorically. The song is inspired by the concept of a black hole, not only as an astronomical phenomenon but also as a symbol of loss, confusion, and the search for meaning in the void.

Concept and Inspiration

This song draws inspiration from the vast and mysterious cosmos, particularly Ton 618, one of the largest black holes ever discovered. The lyrics paint a picture of someone being pulled into the abyss, losing everything they once knew, yet at the same time discovering hope in the most unexpected place.

Genre and Musical Atmosphere

Musically, Black Hole embraces elements of electronic rock, alternative rock, or progressive metal, with a touch of synthwave to create a futuristic and mysterious feel. Heavy instruments such as electric guitars, deep synth pads, and dynamic drums build an atmosphere that enhances the song’s narrative.

Meaning Behind the Lyrics

The lyrics go beyond space exploration—they serve as a metaphor for a personal journey through darkness, whether emotional or spiritual. Yet, within that darkness, there is a small light, a spark that signals the beginning of something new.

This song is perfect for those who love themes of exploration, mystery, and self-discovery, as well as for anyone who has ever felt lost but continues searching for their way home.

Meaning of the Song

"Mirai wo Tomo ni" is a song about hope, perseverance, and the strength of companionship. It conveys the message that no matter how uncertain the future may seem, as long as we have someone by our side, we can overcome any obstacles. The lyrics emphasize trust, dreams, and the courage to move forward together.

The song inspires listeners to embrace change and challenges with confidence, reminding them that the journey toward the future is brighter when shared with someone special. It is a celebration of unity, friendship, and the belief that even in the darkest times, there is always light ahead.

Story Behind the Song

The song follows the journey of two protagonists who set out to create a future of their own. They may come from different backgrounds, face hardships, and even be separated by fate, but they never lose faith in each other.

Their journey represents the struggles and dreams of many—people chasing their ambitions, overcoming fears, and finding strength in the bonds they share with others. The recurring theme of walking together symbolizes how relationships, whether friendships, love, or family, play a crucial role in shaping one’s destiny.

As the song progresses, it reflects their growth, from hesitation and fear to determination and unwavering belief in a better tomorrow. Each lyric captures a step in their path—unlocking the doors to the future, overcoming difficulties, and continuing forward with hope in their hearts.

History of the Song

"Mirai wo Tomo ni" was originally written as a theme for an anime or drama that tells a heartwarming tale of dreams and perseverance. Its uplifting melody and emotionally driven lyrics made it resonate with people facing their own journeys in life.

The song blends elements of J-pop and orchestral music, giving it an inspiring and cinematic feel. Its composition was designed to evoke both nostalgia and motivation, making it suitable for moments of reflection and new beginnings, such as graduations, reunions, or the start of a new adventure.

Legacy and Impact

Over time, Mirai wo Tomo ni became more than just a song—it turned into an anthem of resilience and unity. It is often played during emotional moments, inspiring listeners to hold onto their dreams and cherish the connections they have with others.

Its universal message has made it timeless, serving as a reminder that the future is not something to fear, but something to embrace—especially when walking together with those who matter most.

Worse Than You invites you to look in the mirror when you sense judgement swelling from your eyes and mind after you’ve observed someone else’s actions.

Many of us are on a journey of improving our way of thinking and living, but no matter how good we think we are, there will be times when we fall short of everything we stand for.

Judgement is rooted in fear. When we look at someone who is in a negative cycle or latched onto their victimhood and don’t offer them compassion or understanding, it’s because we see that weakness in ourselves and desire to be rid from it. Another person’s suffering can serve as a reminder of our own flaws which is why their presence can make us feel uncomfortable. When we spew hate or pity onto another, we are either seeing a mirror, the person we used to be, or the person we want to run away from.

As we move into different stages of our lives, it’s important for us to never make the mistake of thinking we’re untouchable. We can do this by checking our egos and offering a helping hand to those who remind us of our past selves. When we lose weight, free ourselves from addiction and laziness, improve our characters, and learn from our mistakes, a part of us will have the fear of going back to who we once were, but rather than feeding our fears, we can silence them by helping others improve themselves.

spinamp-1aa6b273114ae0622f96.description:
Postpartum refers to a period following childbirth, typically the first six weeks to a year. During this time, mothers experience significant hormonal and physical changes while 
also adjusting to the demands of caring for a newborn. It's natural to experience a range of emotions during this period, including:

Baby blues: These are mild mood swings, crying spells, anxiety, and fatigue that affect up to 80% of new mothers and typically resolve within a week or two.
However, some women may develop more serious mental health conditions after childbirth, including:

Postpartum depression: This is a more severe and long-lasting form of depression that affects about 10-15% of mothers. Symptoms include persistent sadness, hopelessness, loss of interest in activities once enjoyed, difficulty sleeping or eating, and difficulty bonding with the baby.

Postpartum anxiety: This involves excessive worry, fear, and physical symptoms like racing heart, shortness of breath, and muscle tension.

Postpartum psychosis: This is a rare but severe condition that can cause hallucinations, delusions, and confusion. It requires immediate medical attention.

Here's a table summarizing the key points:

Condition	Description	Occurs During Postpartum?
Postpartum	Period following childbirth (6 weeks - 1 year)	Yes
Baby Blues	Mild mood swings, short-lived (1-2 weeks)	Yes
Postpartum Depression	More severe, long-lasting depression	Yes
Postpartum Anxiety	Excessive worry, fear, physical symptoms	Yes
Postpartum Psychosis	Rare, severe, hallucinations, delusions	Yes (but less common)

Why it's Important:

It's crucial to distinguish between normal postpartum experiences and symptoms of a mental health condition. If a new mother experiences persistent or worsening symptoms that interfere with daily life or bonding with the baby, seeking professional help is essential.

Here are some resources that can help:

National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI): https://www.nami.org/
Postpartum Support International (PSI): https://www.postpartum.net/
National Suicide Prevention Lifeline (for crisis situations): 988

By understanding the difference between postpartum experiences and mental health conditions, new mothers can get the support they need for a healthy and happy transition into parenthood.

The soundscape is dark, ethereal, and hypnotic, weaving deep chants, ambient hums, and metallic echoes to create the feeling of a presence just beyond reach. The chorus rises like an incantation, a collective voice echoing the unbreakable truth of the blockchain: no rulers, no borders, no chains. As the track fades into static and keystrokes, it leaves behind a lingering message—Satoshi may be gone, but the Phantom’s Code remains, eternal and untamed.

It started as a joke.
One night, after a long studio session, we were messing around talking about all the “secret lives” people live online—late-night searches, private playlists, double lives in the digital age. Someone cracked a joke about "CTRL + Shift + N" being the most-used shortcut in history, and we all laughed… but it hit deeper than expected.

That’s when it clicked.
The idea wasn’t just about watching adult content—it was about owning your desires in a world that tells you to hide them. “Incognito Mode” became a metaphor. A middle finger to shame. A celebration of freedom, pleasure, and self-awareness. We wanted it bold, brash, and sexy—but also smart.

spinamp-a5de1edeaf774f7b7459.description:
Bipolar disorder, formerly called manic-depressive illness, is a mental health condition that causes extreme mood swings that include emotional highs (mania or hypomania) and lows (depression).  These mood swings can affect your sleep, energy, activity level, judgment, behavior, and ability to think clearly.

There are several types of bipolar disorder. The specific type is diagnosed based on the severity, duration, and pattern of your mood episodes. Here are the main types:

Bipolar I disorder:
This is the most severe type of bipolar disorder. It's characterized by manic episodes that last at least seven days or by manic symptoms that are so severe that hospitalization is necessary. Depressive episodes typically last at least two weeks.

Bipolar II disorder:
This type involves depressive episodes that meet the criteria for a major depressive episode, as well as hypomanic episodes, but not full-blown manic episodes. Hypomanic episodes are less severe than manic episodes, but they can still disrupt your life.

Cyclothymic disorder:
This is a milder form of bipolar disorder that involves numerous periods of hypomanic symptoms and depressive symptoms lasting for at least two years. However, the symptoms don't meet the full criteria for a manic or depressive episode.

Bipolar disorder with mixed features:
In this type, you experience symptoms of both mania (or hypomania) and depression at the same time or in rapid succession. This can be a very difficult and unstable state.

Other specified bipolar and related disorders: This category includes presentations that don't neatly fit into the other bipolar disorder diagnoses.
It's important to note that bipolar disorder is a lifelong condition, but it can be effectively managed with medication, therapy, and lifestyle changes. If you think you or someone you know may have bipolar disorder, please reach out to a mental health professional for diagnosis and treatment.

spinamp-7fa2598a334c56b6418e.description:
Mining is the process through which cryptocurrency transactions are gathered, verified and recorded into a digital ledger known as blockchain. The work done by miners is essential for maintaining the integrity of the network and is also responsible for introducing new coins into the system.

Within the traditional banking system, fiat currency is printed and distributed by financial institutions and governmental authorities - but for most cryptocurrencies, the issuance of new coins is not in the hands of centralized entities. Instead, new cryptocurrency units are generated through the process of mining, which follows a predefined set of rules established by the underlying protocol. While the protocol defines what the primary rules are, the so-called consensus algorithms outline how these rules will be followed (for instance, during the validation of transactions).

Taking Bitcoin as an example, the participants involved in the process of mining are called mining nodes (or just miners), and they play a key role in the security of the blockchain network. The job of a miner is to gather unconfirmed transactions from the memory pool and organize them into a candidate block that they will try to validate.

spinamp-ebe9968a2359abaacefb.description:
A blockchain is a distributed ledger with growing lists of records (blocks) that are securely linked together via cryptographic hashes. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, a timestamp, and transaction data (generally represented as a Merkle tree, where data nodes are represented by leaves). Since each block contains information about the previous block, they effectively form a chain (compare linked list data structure), with each additional block linking to the ones before it. Consequently, blockchain transactions are irreversible in that, once they are recorded, the data in any given block cannot be altered retroactively without altering all subsequent blocks.
Blockchains are typically managed by a peer-to-peer (P2P) computer network for use as a public distributed ledger, where nodes collectively adhere to a consensus algorithm protocol to add and validate new transaction blocks.

spinamp-9189329e8ebb6871f6ef.description:
He saw her out past the break, cutting through the waves like she belonged to them. Sun-bleached hair, salt on her skin—she was everything he loved about the ocean, wild and untouchable. He paddled out, hoping to catch the same wave, maybe even catch her eye. She smiled once, just before dropping in, carving her path down the face of the water while he wiped out behind her.

By the time he surfaced, she was already a silhouette against the horizon, drifting farther away with the tide. He told himself he’d see her again, maybe tomorrow, maybe next swell. But as the sun set and the waves flattened, he knew—some things were never meant to stay on shore.

spinamp-3d557c6d6f61d7704625.description:
Short Essay on the song "Suit Up" by Mighty One Man Band


The world may not be getting better. At the time of this writing, wars in various regions on the planet are still waged. The global economy is not doing well. You may not have the life that you dream for.

What we experience in our 3D, physical reality is the result of our thoughts, emotions, and actions. Our collective consciousness also creates the world we live in. 

You don’t like the current state of our planet? You’re not happy with your own life?

What are you gonna do? Does the world need saving?

Maybe you need to be a super-hero? Or maybe you have a savior complex?

No need to have delusion grandeur but ask yourself this question:

WHAT IS YOUR TRUE CALLING?

I wondered how could Stan Lee made all those super-hero characters that eventually became legendary in our global, pop cultures.

On the other hand, Wim Hof stated that you are stronger than you think you are. The key to life is breathing. The effective methods of breathing improve your strength, stamina, and your overall health. That’s how he can endure extreme cold temperatures with no clothes on. That’s how he became the Ice Man. That’s how he became a super human.

Not only Stan Lee or Wim Hof.

Alain Robert, known as “the French Spider-Man” or “the Human Spider” have been climbing skyscrapers since his youth and now he's still doing it in his 60s!

Bruce Lee revolutionized, globalized, and pushed the envelope in martial arts more than anyone has done in history.

Joseph Campbell came up with one of the most profound phrases for humanity: “Follow your bliss”.

The grey alien Bashar (channeled by Darryl Anka) stated that the purpose of life is to follow your highest passion and take that passion to the highest of heights until you can’t take it any further.

And of course, in music, I also have my heroes: J.S. Bach, John Coltrane, Jimi Hendrix, Jaco Pastorius, Stewart Copeland, Eddie Van Halen, Michael Jackson, to name a few.

And don't forget my non-mainstream music heroes as well: Charlie Hunter, Stanley Jordan, Balawan, Hiromi Uehara and many more.

On the other hand, you may also pursue altruism and be like Mahatma Gandhi, Nelson Mandela or Mother Theresa, if that is your true calling.

All these people have “suited up” to become the best version of themselves.

You may think it’s not easy to do the above. To be creative. To find what you love. To be full of passion. To push the boundaries in what you do. To know your purpose in life. To have your own vision. Your own dreams. Your own life. 

Mind you, I was born and raised in an Asian society where everyone there is taught to be ultra obedient and super pragmatic. I’m aware that obedience and pragmatism also exist in the West (I partially grew up in the US) but in Asia it’s on another level. Parents and elders command us to be safe, practical, to be in-the-box and to do do our best to be accepted by society. There is not much room for individuality, creativity or freedom for personal expression. You’ve probably met many Asians who are good in mathematics but no so many of them in the creative arts? This is one of the results of that kind of upbringing. There are exceptions though.

I’m one of those exceptions 😃. I’m that weirdo whom my Asian society don’t understand 😆.

So this is what happened: In my teen years I read a book called “Lateral Thinking” by Edward de Bono. It changed my life. It inspired me to think out-of-the box. It was one of the seeds that propelled the narrative of me eventually becoming the Mighty One Man Band.

Furthermore and still related to the topic, there are knowledge and practices out there that not too many people know. Life hacks that can boost your energy and strength at any time of the day. I too use these techniques to suit up as the Mighty One Man Band. 
This practice has been given many names - Chakra Activation Breathing is one of the most common one. It is an esoteric practice that has been around for thousands of years handed down from the ancient yogis such as UJetsun Milarepa (c. 1052 - c. 1135 CE) to the contemporary practitioners such as José Silva and Dr. Joe Dispenza. 

How do you think I’m able to perform and rock out as the Mighty One Man Band for 2+ hours on stage every time? During the first year of my one-man-band practice, my big brother was one of the few who witness the grind that I put myself in. He told me that I practiced like an olympic athlete. And I still do to this day. I’ve done my 10,000 hours. And more. Sacrifices were made, and again, they still are to this day. And most importantly, I do this all out of love.

When you love something, it’s not easy to explain it. The rush of love energy somehow bypasses the thinking & analytical brain and go straight to the heart as it empowers the heart chakra with infinite light and infinite love.

For me, there’s never been a bigger purpose than suiting up as the Mighty One Man Band. This is my way of “saving the world”. This is the way I “Suit Up”. 

HOW ABOUT YOU?

spinamp-23f149bff41e33bb1cf8.description:
I created the Cosmic Drive album during the months of May - November 2023. It was a hectic period when my partner and I were dealing with the existence of our company and my subsequent hospitalization in addition to everyday joys and worries (track Appendix). The album contains a total of 9 songs, each of which is my personal statement. In each song, I left a piece of myself. The album is tuned to deeper tones, and the bass line will challenge your hi-fi system. It is very melancholic, and it may seem sad to someone, but it is not entirely so. It just tries to keep the mind focused. Therefore, it is suitable to listen to it as a whole during activities where you can think on a larger scale, such as fitness, programming, graphics, artistic activities, and more.

If you like clubby, dirty, and uncompromising sound at 117-124 BPM, deep, tech, minimal, you will definitely enjoy it.

I am convinced that listening to it will inspire you, and you will find a solution to the problem you are currently working on.

spinamp-f3ce319d7ea942e6603f.description:
"The serpent is the earthly essence of man of which he is not conscious. The serpent has the weight of the earth in itself but also its changeability and germination from which everything that becomes emerges." — C.G. Jung

"Serpent" is the sixth single from my album Spectres.

Comprising 13 experimental tracks produced over the last seven years, Spectres is the 28th release in my discography but my first ever completely solo full-length album. While working on this record, I delved deep into Jungian psychology, concepts from which became central to the project. All 13 tracks are named after archetypes—innate, universal forces that shape our experience of the world.

Spectres is also a visual art project. For each track, I crowd-sourced images associated with the corresponding archetype. These image collections were used to train bespoke Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), simulating the complex interplay between individual psyche and collective unconscious. A further GAN was trained on selected outputs from all the previous GANs, uniting the various archetypes to form an integrated Self.

By limiting the training time of these AI models, I found I could achieve results that mirrored the formation of archetypal symbols as I imagine them deep in our collective unconscious: elusive yet powerful forms emerging from abstract swirls of colour. From thousands of outputs, I selected and manually edited one per archetype to create unique artworks for each track. A collection of 144 further images from this project are currently minting on Rarible under the title Spectral Shadows:
https://rarible.com/collection/base/0xb3b592897ba2bd9d06231a56afba9cca9a11619b/drops

Ultimately, Spectres is more than a collection of WAVs and JPGs; it is a dialogue between the personal and the universal, a multidisciplinary exploration of the forces that connect us all. The album has taken me on a transformative seven-year journey through sound, imagery and psyche. In the process, individual and collective experience harmonise, casting a light into the profound depths of human interconnectedness.

Before its official release on 11/23, I'm rolling Spectres out across the web3 ecosystem, with drops on Sound, Zora, Rodeo, Lens and other emerging platforms. In a novel release structure, collectors of individual tracks gain instant access to stream the full album months before its official release. The goal is to push the limits of onchain interoperability to explore what a web3-native album release can look like in 2024.

Cerita:
"Legenda Baru Dimulai" lahir dari semangat seorang pelaut modern yang tak pernah takut melawan ombak kehidupan. Lagu ini menggambarkan perjalanan Kapten Oleng, seorang kapten legendaris yang meninggalkan pelabuhan lama untuk mengejar takdir barunya di tengah luasnya samudra. Setiap petikan gitar dan alunan melodi dalam lagu ini membisikkan kisah perjuangan, harapan, dan tekad untuk menulis babak baru di atas gelombang yang belum pernah dijelajahi. Lagu ini bukan hanya sebuah lagu, tapi simbol tentang bagaimana setiap orang, di manapun berada, bisa menjadi kapten dari cerita hidup mereka sendiri."


Sejarah:
"Diciptakan pada tahun 2025, 'Legenda Baru Dimulai' menjadi karya perdana yang memperkenalkan dunia pada sosok Kapten Oleng di dunia NFT musik. Terinspirasi dari perjalanan panjang para pembuat mimpi yang menolak untuk tenggelam, lagu ini pertama kali dirilis melalui platform Web3 dan langsung mendapatkan perhatian komunitas kreatif global. Dengan kombinasi unik antara nada nostalgia dan semangat masa depan, 'Legenda Baru Dimulai' bukan hanya mengukir kisah Kapten Oleng, tapi juga memulai era baru di mana musik, seni, dan teknologi berlayar bersama menuju keabadian."

**Couplet 1 :**  
*J’écris des barres, mais j’écris pas l’histoire, la vie m’a coupé l’souffle,*  
*La rue m’a appris à compter les étoiles quand y’a plus d’espoir sous les douilles.*  
*Pourquoi j’me bats ? Pourquoi j’cours ? Pourquoi l’amour brûle et s’éteint ?*  
*Pourquoi les potos finissent en taule ou sous terre avant l’matin ?*  

*Maman pleure en silence, dit que Dieu a son plan,*  
*Mais j’vois pas l’dessein, j’vois des murs gris, des chaînes et du sang.*  
*Pourquoi j’fais semblant d’être un roc alors que j’suis en miettes ?*  
*Pourquoi j’mens à mon reflet en disant : "Demain, j’règlerai la dette" ?*  

**(Refrain)**  
*(Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? La pluie tombe mais l’feu reste éteint,*  
*Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? On rit fort pour cacher les craquements.*  
*Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? L’amour part comme un braquage raté,*  
*Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? Personne répond, j’reste scotché.)*  

**Couplet 2 :**  
*J’ai vu l’daron chuter, l’ego plus lourd qu’un coffre-fort,*  
*Maintenant j’triche avec mes peurs, j’vends des rêves en liquide au port.*  
*Pourquoi j’suis là ? Pourquoi j’mens ? Pourquoi j’fais croire que j’maîtrise ?*  
*Pourquoi j’ai l’goût du métal dans la bouche quand la nuit s’éternise ?*  

*Elle m’dit : "T’es un poète", mais j’écris avec du goudron,*  
*Entre les allocs qui s’envolent et les nuits sans horizon.*  
*Pourquoi j’l’aime encore quand ses yeux brillent comme des lames ?*  
*Pourquoi j’attends qu’un signe alors que j’sais qu’on joue au même jeu infâme ?*  

**(Refrain x2)**  
*(Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? La pluie tombe mais l’feu reste éteint,*  
*Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? On rit fort pour cacher les craquements.*  
*Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? L’amour part comme un braquage raté,*  
*Pourquoi ? Pourquoi ? Personne répond, j’reste scotché.)*  

**Pont :**

*La ville respire la sueur, les promesses et les batailles.*  
*Pourquoi j’me lève ? Pourquoi j’tombe ? Pourquoi j’écris ces mots en braille ?*  
*Peut-être qu’la réponse est dans l’silence… Mais le silence me travaille.*  

**Outro :**  
*J’arrête pas d’poser des "Pourquoi", mais la vie, elle balance pas l’bail,*  
*Alors j’graff des questions sur les murs… En espérant qu’un jour, ça tienne.*

spinamp-b999ce36d13fffd4dd58.description:
Darkness has become my only companion since my exile. The castle, once my home, now stands like a ghostly gothic fortress, its spires piercing a moonless sky. I am no longer welcome within its walls, but the shadows of its ruins stretch far beyond its stones. They know me. They call to me. And I still wander through this kingdom that cast me out, a living specter among the living, invisible yet ever-present. The king’s death is but a whisper in the long lament of this cursed land… but a whisper that has awakened something ancient within me.

I don’t need to stand near the throne to sense the scent of blood that permeates the air throughout the realm. It’s everywhere, seeping from the walls, snaking through the narrow streets like a creeping poison. The fearful glances of the villagers, the stifled prayers in the forsaken churches… They know the order is crumbling. The shadow of the king stretches in the dust, and the emptiness he left behind is far worse than his iron grip. Every alleyway, every dilapidated home, echoes with the same terrified murmur: who will be next? And I watch, lurking in the dark, because even in exile, I am bound to this kingdom by a hatred as black as the night itself.

I dwell on the fringes of civilization, roaming the mist-choked woods and moonlit swamps. The bandits and outcasts fear me, whispering my name with morbid reverence. Syralone, the Cursed Wanderer, they say. But they know nothing of me, nothing of this curse gnawing at my soul, nothing of this hunger for vengeance that burns beneath my armor. I did not kill the king, yet the shadows point to me, as if my exile and disgrace are enough to condemn me. Whether I like it or not, I remain their scapegoat… and I can’t help but smile at the thought that, in some twisted way, they’re right.

Because even if I am not the one who took his life, I am far worse. I am the one who hears the secrets no one should ever hear. The one who knows that the king’s death is merely a prelude to something greater, something darker. Something that is slowly awakening from the heart of the kingdom, feeding off its agony. And while the nobles tear each other apart to claim an empty throne, an ancient force stirs. A force I feel pulsing in my veins, answering its call. Like a stray hound that, at last, catches the scent of its prey.

And at the center of this maelstrom of plots and death, there is Her. The Queen of Arkhora, the icy shadow behind the throne. She is more dangerous than all the warlords combined, more cunning than the sorcerers who prowl the cursed forests. She whispers to the darkness, and sometimes, I think I hear my name in her invocations.

Perhaps I am destined to serve once more. Perhaps she, in her calculating coldness, will summon me to defend this decaying kingdom. Me, the banished knight, the cursed blade, called forth for a war that only she can foresee. For it is not the kingdom of Arkhora that is in peril… it is something far greater, far darker. And if the Queen deigns to call me, it will be to unleash the chained beast I have become. The Arkhora I knew died with Damarion. And all that remains are ruins… ruins that, perhaps, still deserve to be defended. Or to be consumed by the madness I carry with me.

spinamp-eb8f568b9bc95941fb79.description:
Blueburst, the musical brainchild of guitarist/vocalist Craig Douglas Miller, defies the notion that it's ever too late to pursue one's passion, resurrecting a music career once thought lost.

After major label interest for his 1990s band, The Reach, never quite panned out, Miller entered a 20 year period of musical hibernation due to untreated clinical depression and writer's block. 

However, a fortuitous meeting with legendary guitarist Marty Willson-Piper changed everything. Inspired by Willson-Piper's guidance, Miller reconstructed his home studio, and completed an album's worth of original songs. 

Together, Miller and Willson-Piper deliver a lush, guitar-based sound rooted in '80s alternative and post-punk, but with a timeless feel. Meanwhile, themes of seizing life's fleeting moments and striving to leave a mark on the world permeate the sonic tapestry. Blueburst's first single, "Vanish," debuted in March 2023, with their debut album, Significance, following up in October 2023. A new album is in the works for 2025.

spinamp-77675318e7fe4e35ea64.description:
Behind the Scene – “Hero.exe”

The creation of Hero.exe began as a tribute to the golden era of NES gaming, but reimagined through a futuristic lens. We wanted to capture the intensity and urgency of boss-level music from classics like Mega Man 2, while fusing it with the punch and polish of modern electronic music. Starting with a tense, cinematic synth intro, we built the track in layers—channeling the spirit of 8-bit arpeggios, but with glitch textures and bold EDM-style transitions.

The composition was structured deliberately to follow a narrative arc: tension, rising action, climax, and resolution—just like a final boss fight. We used a C# minor scale to retain the dark, urgent energy of the original inspiration, and incorporated syncopated rhythms to keep the momentum fierce and engaging. Every sound—from the pixelated leads to the deep sub-bass—was carefully designed to blend nostalgia with innovation. Hero.exe isn’t just a track—it’s a battle cry from the retro-future.

spinamp-41026600a77b1466f119.description:
He first saw her in the early morning light, stepping off the dusty tour bus with city shoes and wide eyes. She laughed at the way the horses nipped at her pockets, charmed by their hunger, oblivious to his. He taught her how to hold the reins, how to sit tall in the saddle, how to let the land stretch out in front of her without rushing to meet it. By the end of the week, she almost looked like she belonged. Almost.

Then, just as quickly as she arrived, she was gone—back to sidewalks and cell towers, to a life that didn’t smell like leather and rain. He kept her bandana tucked in his back pocket, worn soft by the sun, telling himself it was just another summer. But when the season ended, and the bus rolled in with new faces, he still caught himself looking for hers.

spinamp-9c8f00f2d6e21f8289e4.description:
The quatrain by Khayyam you provided is one of his philosophical and profound works that reflects his deep thoughts about life, death, and the concept of time. In this quatrain, Khayyam speaks of those who have traveled the long path of life, noting that none have returned to reveal the secrets of existence.

He emphasizes the fact that no one who has walked this path has come back to explain the mysteries of life and its purpose. Furthermore, he addresses the crossroads of "desire" and "need," inviting the individual not to overlook anything, as time will not return.

This quatrain represents Khayyam's perspective on the transient nature of human life and invites us to contemplate the essence of life, its joys, and the meaning of existence. Khayyam beautifully and succinctly asks whether our coming and going truly hold any benefit.

spinamp-02e128c34119a332ae41.description:
Detroit-bred and Nashville-based singer-songwriter Danny Stevens is ready with his triumphant debut solo LP Better Than You Left Me.
Stevens initially cut his teeth on the indie circuit as the frontman for the seminal pop-rock outfit The Audition - releasing four critically-acclaimed albums, touring the world, and sharing the stage with some of the biggest names in alternative music.
After The Audition, Stevens returned to his roots and began writing the music he had always wanted to create, which references everything from classic Motown soul music and country - to Americana and folk.
While combining these traditional influences together, Stevens also pushes his sound into the modern world by injecting the perfect dose of pop accessibility coupled with tender and vulnerable lyrics that feel both timeless and universally relevant to any listener. "I set out to make an album that sounds like it's for everybody." With an arsenal of songs under his belt, Stevens enlisted the help of prominent Nashville hitmaker and producer Sammy Mitchell (Luke Combs) to lay down the tracks that ultimately became Better Than You Left Me. The result is a hook-laden release that showcases Steven's powerful vocal prowess, a knack for ear-worm melodies, fearless lyricism, and exceptional instrumentation. "I learned to trust myself as a songwriter in this process, and once I did, the floodgates really began to open up" Stevens reflects.

spinamp-1102d9396579af23b538.description:
"I'm So Lonely" is a deeply emotional pop ballad that delves into the profound sense of emptiness that follows a heart-wrenching breakup. The song tells the story of Mia, who finds herself grappling with the stark silence and solitude left in the wake of her relationship's end. Once filled with laughter and shared dreams, her days are now haunted by memories of a love that felt eternal. The lyrics capture Mia's internal struggle as she navigates through the loneliness, longing for the comfort and warmth that have vanished.

spinamp-93256bca3c0651abeebb.description:
Detroit-bred and Nashville-based singer-songwriter Danny Stevens is ready with his triumphant debut solo LP Better Than You Left Me.
Stevens initially cut his teeth on the indie circuit as the frontman for the seminal pop-rock outfit The Audition - releasing four critically-acclaimed albums, touring the world, and sharing the stage with some of the biggest names in alternative music.
After The Audition, Stevens returned to his roots and began writing the music he had always wanted to create, which references everything from classic Motown soul music and country - to Americana and folk.
While combining these traditional influences together, Stevens also pushes his sound into the modern world by injecting the perfect dose of pop accessibility coupled with tender and vulnerable lyrics that feel both timeless and universally relevant to any listener. "I set out to make an album that sounds like it's for everybody." With an arsenal of songs under his belt, Stevens enlisted the help of prominent Nashville hitmaker and producer Sammy Mitchell (Luke Combs) to lay down the tracks that ultimately became Better Than You Left Me. The result is a hook-laden release that showcases Steven's powerful vocal prowess, a knack for ear-worm melodies, fearless lyricism, and exceptional instrumentation. "I learned to trust myself as a songwriter in this process, and once I did, the floodgates really began to open up" Stevens reflects.

General Overseer is a musical piece acknowledging those that contributed in the formation of our DNA and showing the strength they have built around us. spinamp-d428f9612c14c70d8cb5.description:
Prolonged Grief Disorder (PGD), also sometimes referred to as complicated grief, is a mental health condition triggered by the death of a loved one. It's important to distinguish it from normal grief, which is a natural human experience following a loss.

Here's a breakdown of PGD:

Symptoms: PGD is characterized by intense and persistent grief that interferes with daily life. This can manifest as:
Preoccupation with thoughts of the deceased
Intense longing or yearning for the person who died
Emotional pain, numbness, or shock
Difficulty accepting the death
A sense of identity disruption (feeling like a part of you has died)
Difficulty moving on with life
Problems functioning at work, home, and in social situations
Duration: For a diagnosis of PGD, these symptoms must be present for at least:

1 year for adults
6 months for children and adolescents

Severity: The intensity of grief must be significant enough to cause problems in daily life and cannot be explained by cultural or religious mourning practices, or another mental health disorder.
Here are some resources for further information:

American Psychiatric Association:
https://www.psychiatry.org/patients-families/prolonged-grief-disorder

WebMD: https://www.webmd.com/mental-health/prolonged-grief-disorder

639 Hz is a measurement of sound wave vibrations. It indicates 639 cycles (vibrations) per second.
In Alternative Medicine:

639 Hz is associated with a concept called Solfeggio frequencies. These are ancient musical tones that are believed to have specific health and emotional benefits.

It's important to note that scientific evidence supporting specific health benefits of Solfeggio frequencies, including 639 Hz, is limited.
Here are some details about 639 Hz in Solfeggio frequencies:

Claimed benefits: Proponents associate 639 Hz with love, compassion, harmony, and improved relationships.
Uses: It is sometimes used in meditation music or sound therapy aimed at promoting feelings of love and positivity.
Overall, 639 Hz is a sound frequency with interesting applications in alternative medicine. However,  more research is needed to validate the specific claims about its health benefits.

spinamp-fd7e7cc4d3076f88d0ed.description:
Bare with me, this is going to be a longer description than usual. “𝘼𝙪𝙩𝙪𝙢𝙣 𝙋𝙧𝙤𝙡𝙤𝙜𝙪𝙚” 𝙇𝙞𝙫𝙚 @ 𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝘽𝙖𝙨𝙚𝙢𝙚𝙣𝙩 is more than just showcasing myself performing live, but also a celebration of my first year in Web3. I wanted to bring something special and the night of Dec. 9th, 2022 was one I will never forget. It meant a lot for several reasons. 

1.  I wrote this song Sept. 2020, which was a very dark time in my life. I was dealing with the health scares of my dad and grandma, a recent breakup, not getting a job I worked hard for, and overall depression from the pandemic. Although painful times, I wanted to channel that energy and give hope to anyone going through it. 

2. I vividly remember being 17 and one of my homies being an opener at this show. As much as I loved music, before the concert I’d never seen live music. I remember buying a ticket and pulling into this venue The Basement on a Saturday afternoon. Still underage, I got a big ass X on my hand. For the next 4 hours, I was blown away by the sounds I heard and by seeing everyone on stage. Don’t let the name fool you, The Basement is one of the premier concert venues in Columbus, OH, and not everyone gets to play there. It took a decade into my career, but on Dec. 9th, 2022 I got to headline and have some close friends on the bill with me. Such a full-circle moment.

3. The show was emotional for a lot of reasons, but at the end of my set, I legit cried on stage. The moment I  broke down was seeing my parents in the crowd and everything hit me at once. I'm blessed to have folks that believe in what I do and support me. Something I don’t take for granted. I can’t wait to change their lives.

Hopefully, you enjoy the performance and take something away from my story!

Special 1/1 edition featuring an extended narrative and unique sonification elements not included in the limited or open editions of the piece.

Oil and water do not mix. Our biosphere and bodies require water; the Anthropocene as we know it continues to thirst for oil. Can the accelerating breakdown of global climate systems be understood through the lens of this elemental incompatibility?

Constructed with custom sonification tools developed by Pred in Max/MSP, nearly all musical components of the piece are generated from data sets exploring the impact of petroleum on our waterways and ice caps, access to drinking water, hydropower usage, and the price of crude oil.

The goal is not to translate these data points in a literal way, but to use them as starting points for creative exploration. If data is the new oil, can it fuel creativity - not just capture profit? Aside from the biases so often inherent in its collection, data tends to be corrupted in its expression, collapsing reality into abstraction. Composing with arbitrary musical outputs generated from these data sets reflects the dubious nature of much contemporary data usage.

Visualized by the artist in TouchDesigner, freely available drone footage of oil fields and processing facilities are contrasted with aquatic elements, manipulated and depicted in the bounds of a truncated circle, overlaid with pixelated data trails implying the degrading effect of digitized information itself.

spinamp-54ca4f2381730827e7d1.description:
Welcome to Sunset. 

A song that was written for Preseason Training but will not be on the album.

Why?

I’m still getting used to embracing my more tender side of songwriting.

I started making Preseason Training to remember what I was like before getting on Adderall. Before Adderall, I loved basketball and would pour my whole heart into practicing.
When I went to college, I stopped playing competitively (just played pick up at school), and focused on my studies. There was a grief of my former basketball identity that took some years for me to process. At the time, the grief manifested as a severe eating disorder that I received treatment for in 2018. 

At eating disorder treatment, I vividly remember a therapist telling our group that all eating disorders come from not being able to handle your emotions. Hearing that was like watching lightning strike at my feet. Something clicked in me that day and it all made sense. I had been using the eating disorder to not have to feel my emotions. At the time, they were too much to bear. 

Now, I’ve been off adderall for 5 years and feeling more in touch with my body and emotions than I ever thought possible. A lot of this has to do with learning to rest during my luteal and menstrual phase. In web3, we all know how common it is for people to be burnt out or afraid of missing out. I’ve felt very lonely in web3 and have largely been focused on building in person bonds besides releasing these artifacts with CXY and going through the @She__Fi course.

This song is an invitation to sit with yourself and admit how you’re really feeling.


Thank you CXY for making these artifacts possible and helping me bring them to the world!

spinamp-d65dd1c8691f829d9ee1.description:
Born in Brooklyn, New York, I am a first-generation Afro-Latina who grew up as the preacher's daughter. Despite feeling like the outcasted black sheep, I've persevered through life's challenges, including surviving sexual assault and enduring a traumatic kidnapping experience that forced me to leave my job. It was during these difficult times that I made a courageous decision to chase after every dream I'd ever had.

Encouraged by my friends, I finally stepped into the studio after years of singing privately, known only to those closest to me. This pivotal moment opened doors that have led me to where I am today. Through my music, I express myself, sharing the essence of my life and the experiences that have shaped me into who I am—a person who is continually growing and evolving. I am Panarican.


Ever since childhood, I've been filling my notepad with songs and feeling a constant rhythm coursing through my veins – or at least, that's what I'd call it. Some might label it as ADHD, but hey, it's all part of the creative journey, right?

My introduction to the music industry came with my debut release, "Nasty," and it opened my eyes to the unique challenges faced by female artists. That experience fueled my determination to take charge of my own musical journey. I embarked on a quest to record my music and connect with an engineer who could truly understand and embrace my creative vision. And that's when I discovered CQ.

Weeks of relentless effort went into crafting the song that would become "Background." Throughout this journey, I wrestled with imposter syndrome, constantly questioning my abilities. But despite the doubts, I mustered the courage to send it off into the world. "Background" emerged as a testament to that perseverance.

I hold this creation dear to my heart, and I hope it resonates with you too. Your support means the world to me, and I want to express my sincere gratitude for taking the time to read my story. Thank you for standing by me on this musical adventure!

spinamp-f66029d4b985816b2ede.description: A measure of the stability in a system creates blind spots in ensuring values and behaviors such as tolerance, caring, and responsibility. Jang explores the role of art in contributing to the fulfillment of fundamental rights that should be guaranteed universally, in a way that is appropriate and discoverable within the framework of society—who sets the boundaries between normal and abnormal? Is accepting the differences feasible? How can equality be achieved? In response to these questions, the artist seeks to create a specific aesthetic that represents the beauty of his time. Through the ornamentation of bodily prosthetic devices that both compensate for and represent disability, the artist seeks to change the perception that all human beings should be respected for who they are, a condition of existence in which no one should feel ashamed to be human.

I want to reiterate this fact and keep it here that words do not ruin the aesthetics of visual art like visuals do not disturb the imagery where words are present. Like humans, words and visual art have co-existed for centuries.

Poetry has been an integral part of my life and my primary form of art to express, communicate and create what I feel, who I am, what I visualize and how I want my legacy to be about poetry, kindness and love.

This is a token of gratitude to everyone who believes in words and poetry being art.

Have fun and don't forget to read and share a poem with your friends and family today. Bless.

ashwini

About the music:

“Goodbye Alice” is a piece of film score from the Sci-Fi short Oblivio. The music presents the devastating moment when Alice finds out the truth behind her marriage. This piece of music is an award winner for the New York Foundation For the Arts (NYFA) NFT Award Program. “Goodbye Alice" is a part of "Demystifying NFTs: The Award Exhibition" inside Voxel's Metaverse at the BRIDGE++ space from December 15th – December 31st, 2022, curated by Laura Ó Reilly and presented by NYFA.
 
About the film:
 
Oblivio is a Sci-Fi short directed by Dongwei Di and Liyanbing He, produced by Yiwen Gong. The film tells a story of an accidental encounter with an uninvited guest that disrupts Alice's life. As her husband Tom's hidden secret gradually surfaces, Alice finds herself one of the bio-mechanical substitutes of his deceased wife. The film was released by DUST, the Sci-Fi division of independent studio Gunpowder & Sky in 2021. You can watch the film at https://youtu.be/ehUtYYprSTI

About the artist:
 
Haibei Wang is a Chinese composer who has written music for film, music theater, video game, and the concert stage. Her compositions incorporate elements of classical orchestral music, electronic music, jazz music, and Eastern folk influences. Her film scores have premiered at the WorldFest Houston International Film Festival, TIFF, AFMA, SFFILM etc. In late 2020, she worked with Academy Nominated director Chen Kaige to score his short film Baobeier, which was screened in the Chinese TV show Everybody Stand By S2. In 2021, she worked for Grammy nominated composer Frank Wildhorn on his musical No Longer Human, as a music copyist. Around the same time, Oblivio, a Sci-Fi short she scored was released by DUST. In 2022, she won the New Work Grant from Queens Council on the Arts.

Now based in New York City, she completed a Master's degree in composition with a concentration in Screen Scoring from New York University in 2019. She also holds degrees in Concert Composition (B.M.), Organ Performance (B.M.) and Concert Composition (M.M.) from the Shanghai Conservatory of Music. Haibei is currently working on several projects as a composer and orchestrator for multimedia and as a composer assistant for other renowned composers on their studio films.

spinamp-a0d11bf76e669570d33b.description:
The name N¥MPHOSIS comes from the cliché of metamorphosis - mystified as though it were a magical act resulting in something "beautiful" when it’s probably painful, and certainly dangerous; the most interesting part of the process being the gunk that happens in between states, the intermediate state. 

It also comes from nymph, obviously, a term that because of Greek mythology conjures again the "beautiful" but could also be rather regarded as a horror show of a being, an immature, grey sort of exoskeleton coming into full-fledged life. Still preliminary, not completely functional.

When placed together, these weird figures inevitably project narratives. The sickening sticky system of codependence. The inevitability of being wrapped into one another.  Why are we one body, not a system?  Why are discussions of THE BODY centered on the singular?  

The spines are the skeletal nymphosis.  The exoskeleton has been sucked in, which is only possible in the digital iteration, because the physical world is doomed to optical illusions. These works have been painted to appear as though you see through them - we know it's not true, but like some fucked up love, we want to believe in the fantasy.

CONCEPT KRISTIN REGER / krxxx.eth
VISUALIZATION FERNANDO VIAL GÓMEZ
SOUND MATÍAS CONTRERAS

spinamp-ed5d61380c9f723800ba.description:
How many of us suffer from being different. For years we feel locked in existential cages, trying to belong, obeying and adapting ourselves to the wishes of others to avoid criticism and/or discrimination.
Discovering who we are or what we want for ourselves is a slow, difficult, desperate and sad path.
We move back and forth between light and darkness, we fight doubts, we convince ourselves that we are fine and many times we destroy ourselves with pain over and over again.
Some of us manage to get out of these self-imposed or other people's cages and put on masks. We appear happy to avoid explanations or useless lies. Struggling to get out of toxic relationships and unnecessary self-punishments.
It is a process, a construction to one day get out of those cages and those masks and decide to come out into the light and fly like free birds.
We choose to be.

This work has a previous creative process as a background made in 2020 but in this opportunity to minted in Zora was resignified with mixed media (digital drawing, collage and artificial intelligence) to convey the same message that tries to represent the path of struggle, belonging and identity of the LGBTQ+ community.

[rule no.1]
- the double down of these sentiments I have towards my creative capacity and aspirations for autonomy in the professional field has fueled me to gain a new gusto and a mantra: don't wait on no one for your dreams. if there is something you are purposed to do, and you get that itch you can't get rid of, that nagging feeling of disobedience if you don't chase that passion, you gotta double back, run it back and do it. we are given gifts and talents and we must be good stewards over them.

spinamp-1df5ecb4181fb2ff1896.description:
This song is dedicated to all the amazing people who have worked tirelessly to develop the PXNKAP3 project, as well as the tremendous PXNKAP3 community. I wrote this song to be released in celebration of the official PXNKAP3 minting on February 7, 2024. 

The idea to write a song for the PXNKAP3 project and community came to me just a few days prior to the mint date as I began playing around with lyrical ideas related to the project's offerings. I decided to put my writing and production skills to the test to see if I could fully complete the song in just under 3 days, and after a couple of sleepless nights, I successfully reached my goal. 

This song was a ton of fun to write; I wanted to allude to as many of the rich offerings of the PXNKAP3 project as possible while still keeping the song short and to-the-point. It took a few attempts to land on a vocal style for this song, and while I don't typically sing punk rock, I think I found something that worked well enough. On guitar, it was a blast slamming out power chords and trying to keep on tempo for all of the rapid muted downstrokes. The solo was one of the more challenging parts of the song to write since I was under such a time crunch, and I ended up altering part of the song form in order to make the solo fit better. This was also the first time I recorded with my bass guitar as I just recently brought it into my arsenal. And as tedious as it is to hand sequence drums, I really love the process as well as the result. 

I used Reaper as my DAW, and I recorded, edited, and mixed all of the guitars, bass, and vocals in my home studio. Credit goes to my partner for her vocal contribution on the choruses. I used a Studio Projects C1 microphone, a Schecter Diamond Series Garza Signature Edition electric guitar, and a Cort Curbow 52 bass guitar. I hand sequenced the drum parts into a MIDI editor, played through the GetGood Drums Matt Halpern Signature Kit in Kontakt 7. I used a host of plugins for mixing and mastering primarily from Native Instruments, iZotope, Kazrog, and Waves. 

After years of work as a composer, sound designer, and technical audio designer in the games industry, I’m happy to be working on my own personal music again. The minting of this song marks the second song I’ve minted, as well as the second song I’ve produced in 2024, the first being an acapella song titled Art Needs You that I wrote for the Optimism “We Love the Art” on chain art contest. Original minting link here: https://highlight.xyz/mint/659c207641fad46b6bc0e21b

I hope y’all enjoy the song! Thanks for checking it out and for reading a bit about it and my process!

~Joshua

spinamp-c2dafc72dfe6160b5c4d.description:
The Golden Egg = I’ll write a song in French especially for the winner !

I wrote this song back in 2022. There was a lot going on in my life at the time. I was travelling a lot and spent a lot of time in airports. Coming back to France from Canada where I met some friends, a visa problem prevented me from taking my flight. I wrote all the lyrics sitting on the floor at the airport, thinking of the irresistible urge to touch, to see and talk to my girlfriend and of the incredible yearning you could feel in this situation. At the time, all my songs were written in English, but not this one: my Canadian friends find my native language so beautiful, and convinced me to use it in my next song. It was really a revelation in my mind: I began to discover how my own language could be beautiful and full of poetry.
That’s why this is song is so important for me: all my subsequent songs will now follow this way of writing.

Sometimes in life the grass isn't always greener on the other side and what you're looking for is already right in front of you.

A friend once told me, "No matter where you go, be as you are"

Feel free to join LA MUSIQUE DE LI instagram for all updates!
https://www.instagram.com/lamusiquedeli

Much love!

spinamp-2f6c5a827d8a7c6a21cd.description:
Brio is a dynamic music artist hailing from Truckee, CA.  Currently, Brio is working on an ongoing project of experimental Hip-hop, a sound in which he has cultivated over the past few years and is finally bringing to fruition.  Blending a variety of styles, Brio’s music couples unique rap/hip-hop flows with electronic sounds lending to his goal of sharing emotional journeys with his listeners. Emphasizing rhythmic and melodic cadence with his voice in cohesion with his distorted but uplifting beats, Brío’s music seeks to provide a widespread audio experience derived from a broad range of influences.  Brio has been leading the charge for WODA entering Web3 and has also simultaneously been releasing his own personal project as NFTs. 
This song is very personal to Brio. When he was thinking about how he wanted this track to sound he knew that it should start and end melodically with some rap and then in the middle go into some heavier style bass music. Colliding those two genres has been a lot of fun for him lately. He started the song off by talking about his struggles with addiction and then moving into the grief over a friend of his that passed away almost a year ago.  This loss has been highly influential on the entire WODA group’s sound as well. Brio ends the song on a high note by talking about how he has grown and saved himself from the dark that he was in.  Take note of how he moves into this heavier synth building up to a unique “off beat” drop and then brings it back to some soft soothing voices talking about the confusion of being there for himself and someone else at the same time.
Since Brio made this song from a place of processing grief during his studio sessions he wanted to have the crystal represent the person who he lost. And looked so good in. Opal!
Properties : represents amplification, higher hope, and divine purity. These light dancing gemstones are here to boost those feelings of balance and peace and to help you to sift through your thoughts and feelings and throw out what doesn't work. The Opal is also about going deeper spiritually.

This NFT comes with the song and custom single cover of a crystal chosen by Brío. Purchasers of this NFT will receive a limited edition WODA VOL.2 Tee!

spinamp-b4aac2d6558a4d158c2a.description:
It’s been 2½ months since I posted on IG. In this time period, I broke the habit of scrolling and found presence, confidence, and consent in its place 😌🤲🏼 LOVE THAT SH. 

In my experience on Earth thus far, I have noticed that the more I shine, the more likely I am to become a target for other people's projections of pain. My desire is to provide an inspirational template rather than a threatening competition, but I am simply a mirror...I don't get to decide what other people perceive me as. And that's okay.

However, given this experience, my months in "hibernation" (no shows either) have been spent consciously cultivating my emotional resilience and energetic autonomy. I am now very stoked to say that I have developed the internal resources which enable me to rise above others' pain instead of taking it on as my own. It has been exhausting to generate, but so worth it...I feel I am unstoppable. I am light like a leaf, so I can shine like a star. This is my mission; to scale human access to Lightness. 

✧

I received consent from myself to post this video today only after these months of consistently upheld boundaries, both within myself and with the people in my life. I have loved becoming less available. I love saying No. I love being harder to get a hold of. Because of these compassionate boundaries, I am so much more available to ME and to my Guides. The true homies :3

"Jealousy and cruelty roll off of me like water off a duck's back." I am living this affirmation. With the simple intention to be courageous + authentic in my external expression, I knew that whatever I posted today would be able to withstand any energetic projections, because that which is real is enduring. 

✧

Regarding the video itself - I hit some big milestones this past weekend (including moving into an apartment that I've been speaking into existence for the past 9 months!), and felt inspired to offer this letter to my past Selfie. 

Some highlights:
* You don’t owe anybody anything (!!!!!!)
* Trust your gut (🥵🥹 - fool proof)
and another to add in there ::
* Your ability to self-actualize lies in direct proportion to your ability to face your shame 🥲🪞((did u catch that ??) 

✧

What words would you offer your past self ??

The sky is a deep shade of indigo, with stars twinkling in the distance. In the foreground, a group of young people are gathered in a circle, dancing and moving in perfect sync with the music. As the music builds in intensity, the dancers' movements become more frenetic and unpredictable, their bodies blurring together in a kaleidoscope of color and light. The cityscape around them begins to warp and distort, as if the very fabric of reality is being pulled and stretched to the beat of the music.
At the climax of the song, the dancers are surrounded by a swirling vortex of sound and light, their bodies seeming to dissolve into the frenzy of energy around them. The cityscape dissolves into a psychedelic maelstrom, with shapes and colors swirling together in a kaleidoscope of sound and vision.
As the music fades, the dancers re-materialize, their bodies glowing with a soft, ethereal light. They stand in a circle, still moving to the beat of the music, as the cityscape slowly returns to normal. The image fades to black, leaving the listener with a sense of euphoria and wonder at the magic of the music."

spinamp-6835398b3a827bb66662.description:
This art is created using the p5.js library and webgl technology. The code sets up a canvas and defines a draw function that is repeatedly called at a specified frame rate. In the draw function, a number of vertices are randomly generated and stored in an array. The code then sets the fill color, stroke color, and stroke weight to random values and uses the vertices to draw a model on the canvas. The model is rotated slightly on each frame and the canvas is cleared and redrawn.

spinamp-ad91e109200cf673ffdd.description:
Drowning. Underwater. Overwhelmed. Climate catastrophes.

"Spinning Tree" is a remastered vignette initially created as part of the artist's 2021 MFA Thesis installation: As the Past Pulls Away and the Future Begins. This video is an award winner for the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) NFT Program and is part of the "Demystifying NFT's Exhibition" inside Voxel's Metaverse at the BRIDGE ++ space curated by Laura O' Reilly and presented by NYFA. It is Erica Shires' first NFT minted on the Ethereum Blockchain.

Erica Shires is an interdisciplinary artist working with moving images, sound, 3D animation, and taxidermy. Her interests lie in merging the physicality of old media and the natural environment with emerging technologies. Shires recently transformed a 20-year photography career by receiving an MFA in interdisciplinary digital art. Her research-driven art practice centers on death, the obsolescence built into image-making, and our era's growing environmental concerns, specifically — biodiversity and the cascade effects of loss. "✧･ﾟ: *✧･ﾟ:* *:･ﾟ✧*:･" is a demo video of an Instagram filter created during the Meta Spark (fka Spark AR) Open Beta beginning in August 2019. This filter is inspired by posthuman possibilities in web3 where bodies can be glitched to refuse dominant structures. 

Link to try the effect on a mobile device: https://www.instagram.com/ar/2972444792827205/

By minting this piece I'm interested in bringing up the issue of provenance and its perception in the NFT landscape. With AR effects that are made to be shareable on platforms like Instagram, a work is created and made available to users as an experience with a concomitant sense of ownership by the user. In placing instances of augmented bodies on the blockchain, this NFT instantiates one node of queer potential self-expression on an expanding network.

About the artist: Vinh Mai Nguyễn is an artist and writer based in Brooklyn, NY. They are interested in ephemeral acts of bodily augmentation via AR, makeup, nails, and sculpture that glitch the routinized, aiming for illegibility through flux and the practice of incomprehensibility as a liberatory imagining.

"✧･ﾟ: *✧･ﾟ:* *:･ﾟ✧*:･" is a part of "Demystifying NFTs: The Award Exhibition" inside Voxel's Metaverse at the BRIDGE ++ space from December 15th – December 31st, 2022, curated by Laura Ó Reilly and presented by the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) NFT Award Program.

spinamp-18674d1dccf442bb9656.description:
“no matter how this ends i’ll be just fine” is the final track on my EP “things i wanna text u” - a look into my life during one of the biggest heartbreaks I’ve ever experienced. A point that brought me to the lowest point in my mental health I have experienced. The song serves as a reminder to myself, mostly, that no matter how this ends, I’ll be just fine.

But, I didn’t always believe that. I remember clearly one point in the heat of it all where I genuinely questioned if it would be okay. I hadn’t ever experienced that before. I was genuinely concerned about my mental health for the first time ever.

Through this experience, I learned how important it is to take mental health seriously. i learned so much through this journey and want to use this music to help others who are going through something similar. To show them they’re not alone.

That’s why, through this drop, I am donating half of the proceeds to Bring Change To Mind - an organization that is helping to make a change and end the stigma around mental health and mental illness. If you’re struggling, you’re not alone, and I’m here for you.

spinamp-e1adbcf153ae802a1bf1.description:
Special 1/1 edition featuring an extended narrative and unique sonification elements not included in the limited or open editions of the piece.

Oil and water do not mix. Our biosphere and bodies require water; the Anthropocene as we know it continues to thirst for oil. Can the accelerating breakdown of global climate systems be understood through the lens of this elemental incompatibility?

Constructed with custom sonification tools developed by Pred in Max/MSP, nearly all musical components of the piece are generated from data sets exploring the impact of petroleum on our waterways and ice caps, access to drinking water, hydropower usage, and the price of crude oil.

The goal is not to translate these data points in a literal way, but to use them as starting points for creative exploration. If data is the new oil, can it fuel creativity - not just capture profit? Aside from the biases so often inherent in its collection, data tends to be corrupted in its expression, collapsing reality into abstraction. Composing with arbitrary musical outputs generated from these data sets reflects the dubious nature of much contemporary data usage.

Visualized by the artist in TouchDesigner, freely available drone footage of oil fields and processing facilities are contrasted with aquatic elements, manipulated and depicted in the bounds of a truncated circle, overlaid with pixelated data trails implying the degrading effect of digitized information itself. 


Total length: 3:23

Credits:
Audio + Visuals: Noah Pred
Publicly available datasets used for the audio were obtained from:
https://ourworldindata.org/
https://data.noaa.gov/datasetsearch/
https://finance.yahoo.com/
Drone footage used for the visuals obtained from: https://www.pexels.com/ 

Technical details: All sound design, production, and visual outputs by Noah Pred. Created using Max/MSP, Ableton Live, and TouchDesigner. 1080p MP4.

Meta-erotism refers to the exploration of desire and sexuality in unconventional ways, transcending established norms and conventions. In this context, the depersonalization of eroticism aims to highlight gender as a fluid and mutable element, detached from predefined notions of identity.

The NFT artworks in the "Meta Lesbian dating Zora Drops" collection feature abstract and symbolic visual representations of gender questioning. They explore the intersection between desire, identity, and AI, challenging conventional notions of sexuality and relationships.

In summary, the "Meta Lesbian dating Zora Drops" collection is an artistic expression that uses NFTs to explore gender questioning, the relationship between AI and society, and challenges established norms through depersonalized meta-erotism. 'sushi con mate' es este concepto que plasmé en estas 2 piezas, cuya imagen y sonido dan a entender de qué trata. La gracia es que lo puedas interpretar, pero, igualmente, doy mi explicación.
Hace exactamente un año (22/05/2022) me dirigía a preparar mi mate de todas las tardes pero, esta vez, habiendo omitido el almuerzo. Comencé a tomar y, tras unos cuantos, picó el bagre (me dio hambre). No contaba con nada que acompañara el mate (bizcochitos, etc.) por lo que, habiendo sobrado de la noche anterior, y ya teniendo otra comida que cenar definida, opté por agarrar las pocas piezas de sushi que sobrevivían en la heladera.
Esta mezcla tan poco común, y que tan poco atrae, despertó en mí la idea de fusionar estas dos culturas (la japonesa y la argentina) en el aspecto sonoro. Siendo ambos elementos de lo más representativo de cada país. Al menos internacionalmente.
En cuanto al trabajo; ambas piezas llevan, melódicamente, samples de instrumentos japoneses y, rítmicamente, percusiones tradicionales de mi nación.

spinamp-06b7ca1ba9aa0bd96bdc.description:
My inspiration for "Mother" was drawn from her memories of childhood summers spent at her grandmother's countryside home. There, she had discovered the beauty of the natural world – the whispering trees, the babbling brook, and the gentle songs of birds. Yet, intertwined with these organic sounds were the distant hums of machines, a reminder of the modern world's presence even in the midst of serenity.

One afternoon, as rain tapped a gentle rhythm on her studio window, I began to compose "Mother." The track started with soft, ethereal notes reminiscent of a forest at dawn. Gradually, electronic elements were woven in, reflecting the urban pulse that beat in her veins.

As "Mother" evolved, it became a musical tapestry that merged the delicate beauty of nature with the dynamic energy of the city. The melody told a story of unity – of a world where humanity and the environment coexisted in harmony, where the dichotomy between organic and synthetic dissolved into a seamless whole.

As the first notes of "Mother" reverberated in the air, listeners were transported to a realm that was both familiar and otherworldly. The music seemed to conjure memories of childhood adventures in the woods and late-night strolls through city streets. It was a reflection of life itself – a journey of contrasts and connections, of growth and introspection.

And so, "Mother" became a tribute to the world that birthed it, a reminder that amidst the chaos of modernity, the soulful echoes of nature and technology could merge to create something truly beautiful – a testament to the boundless creative power that resided within my music and within us all.

Non-Dystopian is a sci-fi horror music trilogy of mini songs. It was inspired by Historian and Futurist Thinker Yuval Noah Harari and his exploration of the idea of Artificial Intelligence Sidekicks if they were designed to act in the best interest of humans.

In this third part of the trilogy Harari tells the story that even if A.I. sidekicks act in your best interest, you still lose agency over your life.

spinamp-d46e52b25828d38e3587.description:
ERROR MINUS ONE - isn't your typical music experience; it's an immersive dive to the most extreme phase in the creation of this type of music genre. Whether you're a die-hard fan or just curious about music production, consider this your golden ticket to join the sonic adventure behind "ERROR MINUS ONE". It's like a rollercoaster for your ears, going from raw and wild experimentation to the polished beats that make you want to dance. 

The middle section of 'Error Minus Zero' is no longer a secret; it's the focus of this documentary. Experience the ups and downs, the twists and turns, as the artist's ears endure the madness of creating experimental hard techno in 165bpm range. It's like being in the studio, feeling the pulse of each beat and understanding the creative chaos that shapes the final masterpiece. This part is wrapped up in a little story mode, this situation shows that everything can be used and everything can become part of the creative process.

Get ready for an unforgettable journey into the making of the madness!

spinamp-936b130f1c341a6c162a.description:
Elara, known for her daring heists and ability to vanish like smoke, targets the most opulent clock towers in the city, stealing not jewels, but precious Chronoliths - solidified units of time. Yet, she never sells them on the black market. No one knows why.

One night, her target is the workshop of Magnus, a brilliant but reclusive Clocksmith. He suspects a thief, but is unprepared for Elara's quick wit and acrobatic skills. Their confrontation ends with a broken window, a stolen Chronolith, and a reluctant partnership forged.

Magnus believes Elara is a pawn in a larger game, orchestrated by the Collector. He needs her dexterity and knowledge of the black market to track him down. Elara, in turn, seeks Magnus's expertise to unravel the secrets of her clockwork heart, which malfunctions, causing her pain and erratic time jumps.

Their journey takes them across clockwork districts bathed in warm lamplight, down dusty tunnels echoing with gears and chains, and into hidden bazaars where time is bartered like any other commodity. They face clockwork automatons guarding Chronolith vaults, time-bending traps set by the Collector, and the constant threat of Time Wardens, enforcers tasked with protecting the city's temporal flow.

As they delve deeper, their initial distrust melts into grudging respect and then something more. Magnus learns of Elara's past, a childhood shrouded in tragedy where time was stolen from her, fueling her quest to understand and perhaps even reclaim it. Elara witnesses Magnus's desperate desire to save his dying daughter, a wish that pushes him towards unethical experiments with time manipulation.

The climax ensues in the Collector's lair, a labyrinthine fortress fueled by stolen Chronoliths. They discover the Collector's true motive: to break the world's reliance on clockwork time, plunging it into chaos and ruling over the ensuing anarchy.

The final battle is not just physical, but one of choices. Elara must decide whether to use her stolen time to save herself or Magnus's daughter. Magnus must choose between perfecting his time machine and sacrificing his morals. Their decisions, and the unique approaches they take, will determine the fate of the city and their own.

spinamp-b4871e2f2ce5f51d1ddd.description:
Music is my life. 

I started when I was 6, and never stopped. First with the piano, then I added guitar, bass, and full-on music production.

But I never released anything.

So in July 2023 I booked the cheapest flights in Europe, and isolated myself on a remote island off the coast of Turkey with nothing but a midi keyboard, a backpack full of clothes, a laptop and a hard drive. And I got to work.

For 10 days I produced music every day, 9hrs/day. Far away from social distractions and temptations, the only thing I had was a beach bar across the street from my airbnb. Being all alone on this island allowed me to make time to properly focus and start working on my debut album.

When I got back to my hometown of Brussels, I kept that same attitude and isolated myself into my apartment for 5 months. I barely saw my friends, and produced dozens of tracks, some of which made it onto the final record.

As I type these words, I am on a train from Paris back to Brussels, it's 10pm, I spent the day with my mixing engineer. But before I even release the final album, I thought I would give people the chance to own a piece of my life by releasing the untitled, unmixed, and unmastered versions of my tracks.

This is the fifth of 10 tracks that make up the full album.

From Samos to Brussels, by way of Paris, London and the streets of Italy, this record has been with me across Europe and takes inspirations from artists including Ben Böhmer, Fred Again, Underworld, Overmono, and Parra For Cuva.

I hope you like it and you find something you love.

And I hope you love it as much as I loved making it.

Thank you for listening, collecting, or just supporting.

- Roman Müller

spinamp-6621a0ff06a267c53828.description:
Dealing with a broken heart can be an emotionally challenging experience, often leaving one feeling lost and uncertain. However, this difficult period also presents an opportunity for self-discovery and personal growth. By allowing yourself to feel the pain and process the emotions, you can begin to understand your emotional landscape better. 

Take time to reflect on your wants, needs, and aspirations without the influence of your past relationship. It is crucial to prioritize self-care and focus on nurturing your well-being through mindfulness, physical exercise, and pursuing activities that bring you joy.
During this process, you might uncover hidden strengths and talents that have been previously overshadowed. Embrace the newfound freedom to explore these aspects of yourself. Reconnect with friends and loved ones who can offer support and remind you of the love and appreciation you have in your life. It may take time, but gradually, you will find yourself healing and rediscovering the person you truly are, independent of the past relationship. In overcoming heartbreak, you can emerge stronger and more self-aware, ready to embrace life's possibilities with renewed confidence.
